scheme_name: Special Jobs to PwDs - Clerical Assistant
description:
The Special Jobs to Persons with Disabilities Clerical Assistant scheme was launched by the Government of India on December 3, 2019. 

This initiative was introduced to promote the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the workforce. 

The scheme aims to provide job opportunities specifically in clerical positions for individuals with disabilities. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to empower persons with disabilities by providing them with sustainable employment. 

The government has set a target to create at least 10,000 job opportunities for persons with disabilities in the clerical sector within the first three years of implementation. 

The scheme is designed to ensure that at least 5 percent of the total job vacancies in government departments are reserved for persons with disabilities. 

The benefits of the scheme include not only job placements but also skill development and training programs tailored for persons with disabilities. 

Participants in the scheme are provided with a monthly salary of INR 15,000 to INR 20,000 depending on the specific job role and qualifications. 

In addition to the salary, the government also provides a one-time financial assistance of INR 10,000 for necessary work-related equipment. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include individuals aged between 18 and 45 years. 

Applicants must have a recognized disability as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. 

The disability must be at least 40 percent as certified by a medical authority. 

There are no specific educational qualifications mandated for this scheme, but candidates with basic literacy and numeracy skills are preferred. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested candidates must visit the official website of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. 

They must fill out the online application form available on the site. 

The application form requires personal details such as name, age, contact information, and details of the disability. 

Candidates must also upload a copy of their disability certificate issued by a recognized medical authority. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the designated officials. 

Shortlisted candidates are then called for an interview process. 

The interview assesses the candidates' skills and suitability for clerical roles. 

Successful candidates are then provided with job placements in various government departments. 

The timeline for the application process typically starts with the announcement of the scheme on December 3 each year. 

Applications are usually accepted for a period of three months following the announcement. 

Job placements are expected to be completed within six months after the application deadline. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The contact details for the department are available on their official website. 

The department can be reached via email at depwd@nic.in for any inquiries related to the scheme. 

Additionally, the scheme is monitored by various state governments to ensure effective implementation at the local level. 

The government has also partnered with various NGOs to facilitate training programs for candidates. 

These training programs focus on clerical skills such as data entry, typing, and basic computer operations. 

The scheme has been positively received, with an increasing number of applicants each year. 

As of October 2023, more than 5,000 individuals have been successfully placed in clerical positions through this initiative. 

The government aims to expand the scheme to include more job roles beyond clerical positions in the future. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of creating an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities. 

Employers are encouraged to provide reasonable accommodations to support employees with disabilities. 

The government conducts regular workshops and awareness programs to educate employers about the benefits of hiring persons with disabilities. 

Statistics show that employment rates for persons with disabilities have improved since the launch of this scheme. 

The scheme also aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 8, which promotes decent work and economic growth. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years. 

This budget is aimed at supporting training programs, job placements, and financial assistance for candidates. 

The Special Jobs to Persons with Disabilities Clerical Assistant scheme is a significant step towards enhancing the employability of persons with disabilities in India. 

It addresses the barriers faced by individuals with disabilities in accessing employment opportunities. 

The scheme not only provides financial independence but also boosts the confidence of individuals with disabilities. 

By facilitating job placements, the government aims to reduce the unemployment rate among persons with disabilities, which currently stands at approximately 70 percent. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Indian government to promote inclusivity and diversity in the workforce. 

It reflects the commitment of the government to uphold the rights of persons with disabilities as enshrined in the Constitution of India. 

Overall, the Special Jobs to Persons with Disabilities Clerical Assistant scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at empowering individuals with disabilities through meaningful employment opportunities. 

By providing targeted support and resources, the scheme seeks to create a more inclusive society where everyone has the opportunity to contribute to the economy. 

The ongoing efforts to expand and improve this scheme will play a crucial role in shaping the future of employment for persons with disabilities in India. 

The government continues to seek feedback from participants and stakeholders to enhance the effectiveness of the scheme. 

This feedback mechanism is essential for making necessary adjustments to the program to better serve the needs of persons with disabilities. 

The Special Jobs to Persons with Disabilities Clerical Assistant scheme exemplifies the government's dedication to fostering an inclusive workforce that values diversity and equal opportunity for all.
